_note: Expanded by scripts/generate_rw_content.py from authored corpora. Original items.

questions.stimulus: Far from ______ the debate, the new data gave each side fresh material.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: 'Far from' contrasts with both sides gaining material, whose opposite is resolving the dispute.

questions.stimulus: Camels can drink over a hundred litres of water in a few minutes. ______ they can go for days without drinking at all.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: Drinking enormous amounts and needing none are opposed behaviours, calling for contrast.

questions.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student took the following notes:

- Ada Lovelace worked with Charles Babbage in the 1840s.
- She wrote notes on his proposed Analytical Engine.
- Her notes include an algorithm for computing Bernoulli numbers.
- She also argued the machine could manipulate symbols, not just numbers.
questions.stem: The student wants to emphasize the conceptual leap in Lovelace's notes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: Lovelace wrote extensive notes on the Analytical Engine.
Lovelace's notes include an algorithm for Bernoulli numbers.
Lovelace argued that the Analytical Engine could manipulate symbols rather than merely calculate, anticipating uses beyond arithmetic.
Ada Lovelace worked with Charles Babbage in the 1840s.

questions.rationale: The conceptual leap is the claim about symbols; the algorithm and the collaboration are context.

questions.stimulus: Bamboo reaches full height in a single growing season. ______ it is harvested on a far shorter cycle than hardwood timber.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: Fast growth causes the short harvest cycle, so a causal transition fits.

questions.stimulus: Most antibiotics target features unique to bacterial cells. ______ they leave human cells largely unharmed.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The targeting explains the safety, so the transition signals result.

questions.stimulus: The statute defines the offence in unusually broad terms. ______ prosecutors have charged it in fewer than a dozen cases in thirty years.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: Broad definition would predict frequent charges; the rarity is a concession against that expectation.

questions.stimulus: The manuscript's marginalia are written in at least three hands. ______ the volume passed through several readers before reaching the library.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: Three hands supports an inference about the book's history, which 'Evidently' marks.

questions.stimulus: Sea ice reflects most of the sunlight that strikes it. ______ open water absorbs it.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: Reflecting and absorbing are opposed behaviours, so contrast is required.

questions.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student took the following notes:

- Lake Nyos is a crater lake in Cameroon.
- Carbon dioxide seeps into its depths from magma below.
- In 1986 the lake released a large cloud of the gas.
- The cloud suffocated more than 1,700 people.
- Degassing pipes were installed beginning in 2001.
questions.stem: The student wants to emphasize the measure taken to prevent a recurrence. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: Lake Nyos is a crater lake in Cameroon fed by volcanic gas.
Carbon dioxide seeps into Lake Nyos from magma below.
Since 2001, degassing pipes have vented carbon dioxide from Lake Nyos to prevent another release like the one that killed more than 1,700 people in 1986.
In 1986 Lake Nyos released a cloud of carbon dioxide.

questions.rationale: Only one choice describes the preventive measure rather than the hazard or the disaster.

questions.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student took the following notes:

- Coffee rust is a fungal disease of coffee plants.
- It first devastated plantations in Ceylon in the 1870s.
- Growers there replaced coffee with tea.
- Ceylon tea remains a major export today.
questions.stem: The student wants to emphasize the long-term economic consequence of the outbreak. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: Ceylon growers replaced their coffee plants with tea.
After coffee rust destroyed Ceylon's plantations in the 1870s, growers switched to tea, which remains a major export today.
Coffee rust reached Ceylon in the 1870s.
Coffee rust is a fungal disease that attacks coffee plants.

questions.rationale: The long-term consequence requires connecting the outbreak to tea's continuing importance.

questions.stimulus: A machine-learning model trained to detect pneumonia from chest X-rays performed excellently on its training hospital's images and poorly elsewhere. Investigators found the model had learned to read a small metal token that one hospital's technicians clipped to the film of patients admitted through the emergency department.
questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: The training hospital therefore had unusually accurate radiologists.
The model therefore requires higher-resolution images to work.
The model's apparent skill rested on a marker correlated with illness rather than on features of the lungs themselves.
Pneumonia therefore cannot be detected from chest X-rays.

questions.rationale: Reading the token rather than the anatomy explains both the strong in-hospital result and the failure elsewhere.

questions.stimulus: The discovery was ______ rather than planned: the team had been searching for something else entirely.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Finding something while looking for something else is an incidental discovery.

questions.stimulus: Excavations at the site have recovered thousands of animal bones but almost no cooking hearths. ______ the assemblage may represent butchery carried out for consumption elsewhere.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The inference draws on both observations at once, which 'Taken together' signals.

questions.stimulus: The recipe is ______, calling for only three ingredients and one pan.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Three ingredients and one pan describes simplicity.

questions.stimulus: The library's collection of maps is ______, spanning six centuries and four continents.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Six centuries and four continents describes great range, which 'extensive' names.

questions.stimulus: Standard accounts credit the printing press with the rapid spread of vernacular literature. ______ manuscripts in vernacular languages circulated widely for a century beforehand.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The second sentence corrects the standard account rather than following from it.

questions.stimulus: Peer review is often described as a filter that keeps error out of the literature. It works better as a filter on presentation: reviewers see a manuscript, not a laboratory, and can judge whether an argument follows from the data shown without being able to verify that the data were collected as described.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.text: To refine a common description of what peer review can and cannot check
To compare peer review across scientific disciplines
To argue that peer review should be abolished
To describe the history of the peer review system

questions.rationale: The text replaces 'filter on error' with 'filter on presentation' and explains the limit reviewers work under.

questions.stimulus: The Mary Rose sank in 1545 and lay under silt for four centuries. The silt sealed out oxygen, so the timbers and even the crew's woollen caps survived. When the hull was raised in 1982 it brought up an inventory of Tudor daily life that no document records.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Tudor documents contain detailed inventories of shipboard life.
Raising the hull in 1982 damaged much of the cargo.
The Mary Rose was the largest warship of its era.
Oxygen-free silt preserved objects that written sources never described.

questions.rationale: The passage attributes preservation to the oxygen-free silt and stresses that the finds are undocumented elsewhere.

questions.stimulus: The committee's endorsement was ______, hedged with so many conditions that it amounted to a refusal.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: An endorsement in name only, undercut by conditions, is nominal.

questions.stimulus: The study's conclusions are ______ by its sample, which was drawn entirely from one hospital.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: A sample from a single hospital limits how far conclusions extend; 'circumscribed' names that limiting.

questions.stimulus: Although the museum bills the collection as complete, it is in fact ______: three of the panels are copies.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Some panels being copies makes the collection assembled from mixed sources rather than uniformly original.

questions.stimulus: Musicologist Farah Nasser argues that the sudden popularity of the twelve-string guitar in the 1960s owed less to its sound than to its visibility: a handful of televised performances put the instrument in front of millions.
questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most strongly support Nasser's argument?

choices.text: Sales of twelve-string guitars rose sharply in the weeks immediately following each televised performance, with no change in their price or design.
Twelve-string guitars produce a fuller sound than six-string models.
Twelve-string guitars were more difficult to tune than six-string models.
Several prominent musicians preferred twelve-string guitars.

questions.rationale: Nasser attributes popularity to visibility, so evidence must tie sales to the broadcasts rather than to the instrument's qualities.

questions.stimulus: The artist's late work is notably ______, stripping away the ornament that filled her early canvases.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Stripping away ornament produces austerity; 'cluttered' describes what was removed.

questions.stimulus: The two accounts are not contradictory so much as ______: each describes a different stage of the process.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Describing different stages means the accounts fit together rather than conflict.

questions.stimulus: Neural networks and human learners both improve with practice on a task. ______ the resemblance breaks down under distribution shift, where humans generalize and networks often do not.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The second sentence limits the analogy just drawn, marking where it stops holding.

questions.stimulus: Her prose is ______ without being obscure: every sentence rewards a second reading but none requires one.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Rewarding rereading without requiring it describes compression, which 'dense' names, while 'obscure' is ruled out.

questions.stimulus: Rather than ______ the conflicting accounts, the historian presents both and explains why they differ.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: The contrast is with presenting both accounts separately, so the rejected option is forcing them into agreement.

questions.stimulus: Standard histories of vaccination begin with Edward Jenner in 1796. Variolation, deliberate exposure to a mild smallpox strain, was practised in China and the Ottoman Empire generations earlier and reached Britain through Lady Mary Wortley Montagu's advocacy in the 1720s. Jenner's contribution was safer method, not first principle.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Lady Mary Wortley Montagu invented the practice of variolation.
Deliberate immunization predates Jenner, whose advance was in safety rather than in the underlying idea.
Variolation was more effective than vaccination.
Jenner's work in 1796 has been shown to be fraudulent.

questions.rationale: The text places variolation earlier and characterizes Jenner's role as a safer method, not the original insight.

questions.stimulus: The alloy resists corrosion and weighs a third less than steel. ______ its cost has confined it to aerospace applications.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: Advantages are followed by a limitation that overrides them, so a concessive contrast is needed.

questions.stimulus: The Dust Bowl is often explained by drought alone. Soil scientist Halima Osei points out that droughts of comparable severity struck the same counties in the 1890s without stripping the topsoil. What differed by the 1930s was the depth and extent of mechanized ploughing, which had broken the deep-rooted grass that held the soil in place.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Osei argues that the 1930s drought was more severe than earlier ones.
Osei attributes the Dust Bowl's severity to ploughing practices rather than to drought by itself.
Osei believes mechanized ploughing increased crop yields.
Osei denies that drought occurred in the 1930s.

questions.rationale: The 1890s comparison isolates ploughing, not drought, as the differing factor.

questions.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student took the following notes:

- The kakapo is a flightless parrot native to New Zealand.
- It is nocturnal.
- Adults can weigh up to 4 kilograms.
- Fewer than 250 individuals remain.
questions.stem: The student wants to emphasize the kakapo's conservation status. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: Adult kakapo can weigh up to 4 kilograms.
The kakapo is flightless and nocturnal.
The kakapo is a nocturnal parrot native to New Zealand.
Fewer than 250 kakapo remain, making the flightless New Zealand parrot one of the world's rarest birds.

questions.rationale: Only the choice citing the remaining population addresses conservation status.

questions.stimulus:
Researchers recorded nesting success for a bird species at four distances from a road.

| Distance from road | Nests fledging young |
|---|---|
| 50 m | 31% |
| 200 m | 54% |
| 500 m | 68% |
| 1000 m | 70% |

They concluded that road proximity depresses nesting success, with the effect levelling off beyond a few hundred metres.
questions.stem: Which choice best uses data from the table to support the researchers' conclusion?

choices.text: Success at 200 m was 54%, higher than at 50 m.
Nests closest to the road were least successful, at 31%.
Nests 1000 m from the road fledged young 70% of the time.
Success climbed steeply from 31% at 50 m to 68% at 500 m, then changed little between 500 m and 1000 m.

questions.rationale: The conclusion has two parts, a decline near roads and a plateau further out, and only one choice reports both.

questions.stimulus: The festival was scheduled for the town square. ______ heavy rain forced organizers to move it indoors.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The plan and what happened conflict, so contrast is required.

questions.stimulus: The company projected that the new plant would open in March. ______ construction was still unfinished the following December.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The outcome contradicts the projection, which 'In fact' introduces.

questions.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student took the following notes:

- Honey does not spoil.
- Sealed jars have been found in ancient tombs.
- Its low water content inhibits bacteria.
- It is also highly acidic.
questions.stem: The student wants to explain why honey does not spoil. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: Sealed jars of honey have been found in ancient tombs.
Honey does not spoil, even after thousands of years.
Honey is both acidic and low in water.
Honey resists spoilage because its low water content and high acidity together inhibit bacteria.

questions.rationale: The goal is causal, and only one choice names both properties as the reason.

questions.stimulus: Archaeologist Sunil Rao proposes that a settlement's unusual grain-storage pits were communal rather than household property. Critics note that communal and household storage can look identical once abandoned.
questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most weaken the critics' objection?

choices.text: The pits were all dug to approximately the same depth.
The pits are clustered in a single open area at the settlement's centre, away from every identified dwelling.
The pits remained in use for several generations.
Grain residue in the pits comes from several different crops.

questions.rationale: Placement away from dwellings and grouped centrally distinguishes communal from household storage, which is exactly what the critics say cannot be told apart.

questions.stimulus: A researcher claims that providing free public transit passes increases the number of trips people take to medical appointments.
questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researcher's claim?

choices.text: The passes were valid on buses but not on the commuter rail line.
Most pass recipients reported being satisfied with the programme.
Clinics in districts where passes were distributed recorded a rise in kept appointments, while clinics in districts without passes recorded no change.
Public transit ridership rose overall in the year the passes were introduced.

questions.rationale: The claim links passes to medical trips specifically, and only the clinic comparison isolates that effect against a control.

questions.stimulus: Octopuses have no bones, and can squeeze through any opening larger than their beak, the single rigid part of their body. Aquarium keepers size lids not by the animal's bulk but by that one measurement.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Octopuses are the most flexible animals in the ocean.
An octopus's beak, not its overall size, determines the gaps it can pass through.
Aquarium keepers prefer lids made of rigid material.

questions.rationale: The text identifies the beak as the limiting rigid part and notes keepers size lids by it.

questions.stimulus: A drug performed well in trials conducted at high-altitude clinics but showed no benefit at sea level. The compound's proposed mechanism depends on binding to haemoglobin, and residents at altitude carry substantially more haemoglobin than sea-level populations.
questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Haemoglobin levels therefore have no bearing on the drug's action.
Altitude therefore causes the condition the drug treats.
The drug's apparent effectiveness may depend on the elevated haemoglobin levels found at altitude rather than on altitude itself.
The drug is therefore ineffective under all conditions.

questions.rationale: The mechanism runs through haemoglobin, which is elevated at altitude, so the binding target rather than elevation explains the pattern.

questions.stimulus: The witness's testimony was ______ on the central point: he had given three different times for the same event.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Three different times for one event is self-contradiction, which 'inconsistent' names.

questions.stimulus: Venice was built on soft mud, which cannot bear the weight of stone. Its builders drove millions of wooden piles into the seabed until they reached firmer clay beneath. Submerged in oxygen-poor water, the wood never rotted, and much of it still holds the city up.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Venice stands on wooden piles that have survived because they sit in oxygen-poor water.
Venice's builders preferred wood to stone for aesthetic reasons.
Venice was built on ground too soft to support any structure.
Wooden piles are stronger than stone foundations.

questions.rationale: The text explains the soft ground, the piles driven to firmer clay, and why the wood survived.

questions.stimulus: The Voynich manuscript has resisted every attempt at translation since its rediscovery in 1912. Statistical analyses show its symbol frequencies behave like those of a natural language rather than random noise, yet no proposed decipherment has been reproducible. The text is either an unknown script or an unusually sophisticated hoax.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: The manuscript was written in a language now extinct.
The manuscript's linguistic statistics rule out randomness but have not settled whether it encodes a real language.
The manuscript is almost certainly an elaborate hoax.
Statistical analysis has produced a reproducible decipherment.

questions.rationale: The text reports language-like statistics, no reproducible decipherment, and two remaining possibilities.

questions.stimulus: Aluminium is abundant in the earth's crust. ______ it was once more valuable than gold, because separating it was so difficult.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: Abundance and high value are in tension, so the transition must mark contrast.

questions.stimulus: Most spiders build a fresh web each day. The bolas spider does not build one at all. It dangles a single silk line tipped with a sticky globule and swings it at passing moths, which it attracts by mimicking their scent.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.text: To argue that bolas spiders are more efficient hunters than other spiders
To explain how spiders produce silk
To describe a hunting method that departs from typical spider behaviour
To compare the diets of different spider species

questions.rationale: The text sets up the usual pattern, marks the bolas spider as an exception, and details that exception.

questions.stimulus: The prosecution's case rested on ______ evidence, since no witness had seen the act itself.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Evidence in the absence of an eyewitness to the act is circumstantial, the opposite of direct.

questions.stimulus: The negotiator's manner was ______, giving no hint of which concession she would accept.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Giving no hint of her position describes an unreadable manner.

questions.stimulus: The first draft of the constitution ran to ninety pages. ______ the ratified text fits on four.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The contrast between draft and final length is resolved chronologically by 'In the end'.

questions.stimulus: The lighthouse was automated in 1987. ______ no keeper has lived on the island since.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: Automation caused the end of resident keepers.

questions.stimulus: The mayor's speech was deliberately ______, lasting under four minutes and naming only one policy.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Under four minutes and one policy describes shortness, which 'brief' names.

questions.stimulus: Her account of the voyage is ______: she recorded the weather every four hours for two years.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Recording weather every four hours for two years is exhaustive detail.

questions.stimulus: Some moths have evolved ears tuned to the frequencies bats use for echolocation. On islands that bats never colonized, related moth species have the same ear structures but show no behavioural response when those frequencies are played.
questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Ears therefore evolve only in the presence of predators.
Bats therefore never used echolocation on those islands.
The hearing structures appear to persist without the evasive behaviour once the predator is absent.
The island moths therefore cannot hear at all.

questions.rationale: The islands preserve the structures but lose the response, so anatomy outlasts the behaviour when the pressure is gone.

questions.stimulus: A publisher found that novels with the author's name in larger type sold better, and concluded that type size drives sales. The publisher had reserved the largest type for its already best-selling authors.
questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Type size therefore has a stronger effect than the publisher realized.
Best-selling authors therefore prefer smaller type.
The correlation is therefore better explained by the authors' existing popularity than by the typography.
The publisher therefore should reduce type size on all covers.

questions.rationale: Large type was assigned to authors who already sold well, so prior popularity confounds the comparison.

questions.stimulus: A student claims that street trees measurably reduce summer temperatures in city neighbourhoods.
questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the student's claim?

choices.text: Street trees in the city are most commonly planted in spring.
Residents report that tree-lined streets are more attractive.
Street trees require regular pruning to remain healthy.
Sensors recorded afternoon temperatures three degrees lower on tree-lined streets than on comparable treeless streets nearby.

questions.rationale: The claim is about measured temperature reduction, and only the sensor comparison measures it.

questions.stimulus: The report was ______ enough that the council read it in a single sitting.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Reading it in one sitting indicates shortness; 'exhaustive' would suggest the opposite.

questions.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student took the following notes:

- The Rosetta Stone was found in 1799.
- It carries the same decree in three scripts.
- The scripts are hieroglyphic, Demotic, and Greek.
- Scholars used the Greek to decipher the hieroglyphs.
questions.stem: The student wants to explain how the stone made decipherment possible. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: Because the stone repeats one decree in hieroglyphic, Demotic, and Greek, scholars could use the Greek to decipher the hieroglyphs.
The Rosetta Stone carries a decree in three scripts.
The Rosetta Stone was found in 1799.
The Rosetta Stone is written partly in Greek.

questions.rationale: Only the choice linking the known script to the unknown one explains decipherment.

questions.stimulus: Field recordings captured the bird's song across six regions. ______ the dialects proved distinct enough that researchers could identify a bird's origin by ear.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The second sentence strengthens and confirms the first rather than opposing it.

questions.stimulus: The museum offers free entry on the first Sunday of each month. ______ visitors should expect long queues on those days.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: Free entry causes the crowds, so the transition must signal result.

questions.stimulus: The pistol shrimp hunts without touching its prey. Snapping one oversized claw shut produces a bubble that collapses so violently it generates a shock wave, stunning small fish at a distance of several centimetres.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: The pistol shrimp has one claw larger than the other.
Small fish are the pistol shrimp's only prey.
The pistol shrimp stuns prey at a distance using a shock wave produced by its claw.
The pistol shrimp is among the loudest animals in the ocean.

questions.rationale: The text describes the claw, the collapsing bubble, and the resulting shock wave that stuns prey at a distance.

questions.stimulus: The teacher's explanation was ______, and several students asked her to repeat it.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Students needing it repeated indicates the explanation was unclear.

questions.stimulus: A pottery workshop's output can often be traced by the clay it used. Vessels excavated at an inland fortress match, in mineral composition, clay beds found only on a coastal plain two hundred kilometres away. No kiln has been found at the fortress.
questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: The coastal plain was most likely settled from the fortress.
The vessels were most likely made on the coastal plain and transported inland.
The mineral analysis is most likely mistaken.
The fortress most likely imported clay and fired it on site.

questions.rationale: Coastal clay plus no kiln at the fortress points to manufacture at the source and transport of finished vessels.

questions.stimulus: The essay is valuable less for its conclusions, which are ______, than for the questions it raises.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: 'Less for X than for Y' downgrades the conclusions relative to the questions, so the conclusions are ordinary.

questions.stimulus: Ecologists have long treated invasive species as uniformly damaging. Botanist Ingrid Sorensen resists the framing without denying the harm. On degraded land where native seed banks are exhausted, she argues, fast-colonizing non-natives can stabilize soil and shade out bare ground, creating conditions under which natives can later be reintroduced. The label describes an origin, not an effect.
questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the final sentence in the text?

choices.text: It concedes a limitation in Sorensen's argument.
It restates the conventional ecological position.
It states the conceptual point the preceding example was offered to establish.
It introduces a new line of evidence about seed banks.

questions.rationale: 'The label describes an origin, not an effect' generalizes from the degraded-land case into the claim the passage is making.

questions.stimulus: Because the fossil was so ______, researchers could identify individual feather barbs.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Seeing individual barbs requires exceptional preservation; 'fragmentary' contradicts it.

questions.stimulus: The survey found broad public support for the measure. ______ turnout at the referendum was among the lowest on record.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: Support and low turnout are in tension, calling for a concessive contrast.

questions.stimulus: Economists have long modelled traffic fatalities as falling with vehicle safety features. Policy analyst Bram de Vries notes that pedestrian deaths in several countries rose over the same decades in which occupant deaths fell, and that the vehicles credited with protecting occupants grew heavier and taller. Safety, on his account, was redistributed rather than created.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: De Vries believes heavier vehicles are safer for everyone.
De Vries argues that pedestrian deaths are undercounted.
De Vries argues that gains in occupant safety came partly at pedestrians' expense rather than representing a net reduction in harm.
De Vries denies that vehicle safety features protect occupants.

questions.rationale: Falling occupant deaths alongside rising pedestrian deaths supports the 'redistributed rather than created' conclusion.

questions.stimulus: The regulations are ______, leaving inspectors to decide case by case what counts as compliance.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Leaving decisions to inspectors indicates rules that do not specify outcomes.

questions.stimulus: The record is ______ for the crucial decade: two ledgers survive, and neither covers a full year.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Two partial ledgers constitute broken, incomplete evidence.

questions.stimulus: The reforms were ______ rather than systemic, addressing individual complaints as they arose.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Addressing complaints one at a time contrasts with systemic change; 'piecemeal' names that fragmentary approach.

questions.stimulus: The account is ______ in its detail yet strangely uninformative about the author's own role.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: 'Yet' contrasts abundant detail with a specific silence, so the first term must mean extremely thorough.

questions.stimulus: Lead isotope ratios differ measurably between ore fields. Bronze artefacts from a Mediterranean shipwreck carry ratios matching a single Anatolian source, while the tin in the same objects matches deposits in Cornwall, some four thousand kilometres away.
questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Anatolian and Cornish ores therefore share a common origin.
The objects therefore combine metals drawn from opposite ends of a long-distance exchange network.
The artefacts were therefore manufactured in Cornwall.
The isotope analysis is therefore unreliable for tin.

questions.rationale: Copper from Anatolia and tin from Cornwall in one object implies materials travelling across a wide network.

questions.stimulus: The evidence for the hypothesis remains ______, resting on a single unreplicated experiment.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: A single unreplicated experiment makes support thin, which 'tenuous' names.

questions.stimulus: Digitizing the collection made it searchable from anywhere. ______ it drew scholars away from the reading room, whose staff had answered questions no catalogue anticipates.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: A benefit and a simultaneous cost call for a transition marking concurrence rather than result.

questions.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student took the following notes:

- Nauru was once among the richest countries per capita.
- Its wealth came from phosphate deposits.
- The deposits were largely exhausted by the 1990s.
- Mining left about 80 percent of the island uninhabitable.
- The country now imports nearly all its food.
questions.stem: The student wants to emphasize the lasting cost of the island's phosphate economy. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: Nauru's wealth came from its phosphate deposits.
Nauru's phosphate deposits were exhausted by the 1990s.
Phosphate mining left roughly 80 percent of Nauru uninhabitable and the country dependent on imported food once the deposits ran out.
Nauru was once among the richest countries per capita.

questions.rationale: The lasting cost is the ruined land and import dependence, not the former wealth or the timeline.

questions.stimulus: Far from being ______, the treaty's language was chosen to leave each signatory room to interpret it.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: 'Far from being' contrasts with language leaving room for interpretation, whose opposite is precision.

questions.stimulus: The policy was ______ from the start, since the agency charged with enforcing it had no inspectors.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Having no inspectors is precisely what makes enforcement impossible.

questions.stimulus: Her argument was ______: each claim followed from the one before it.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Claims following from one another is coherence; 'disjointed' is the opposite.

questions.stimulus: His influence on the field is ______, visible in the vocabulary his critics use to attack him.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Even opponents using his vocabulary shows influence that has spread everywhere.

questions.stimulus: The reforms were ______ by the very officials charged with carrying them out.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: 'By the very officials charged with carrying them out' signals an ironic reversal, so the reforms were blocked.

questions.stimulus: The metric system was designed to be reproducible from nature: the metre was defined as a fraction of the earth's meridian. That definition proved impractical to check, and the metre is now fixed by the distance light travels in a specified fraction of a second.
questions.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.text: It presents an original definition and then explains what replaced it and why.
It argues that the metric system should be abandoned.
It describes how the earth's meridian was first measured.
It compares the metric system with older measurement systems.

questions.rationale: The text gives the original meridian-based definition, notes it was impractical, and states the current one.

questions.stimulus: Critics have read the painting's unfinished corner as evidence of the artist's failing health. ______ X-ray imaging reveals a completed passage beneath, deliberately scraped away.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The imaging contradicts the critics' reading, so contrast is needed.

questions.stimulus: The vaccine trial recruited participants across eleven countries. ______ its results are more readily generalized than those of single-site studies.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: Broad recruitment causes the improved generalizability.

questions.stimulus: Desert plants face a dilemma: the pores they open to take in carbon dioxide also release water. Many cacti open theirs only after dark, storing the gas until daylight allows photosynthesis to proceed.
questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Desert plants therefore keep their pores permanently closed.
Opening the pores at night therefore reduces the water a cactus loses.
Cacti therefore photosynthesize more efficiently at night.
Cacti therefore do not require carbon dioxide.

questions.rationale: Water loss through open pores is the stated cost, and darkness is cooler, so night opening limits that loss.

questions.stimulus: Sourdough relies on wild yeast already present in flour and air. ______ it requires no commercial yeast at all.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: Relying on wild yeast causes the absence of commercial yeast.

questions.stimulus: The company attributed the outage to an unforeseeable hardware fault. ______ an internal review found that the same component had failed twice in the preceding year.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The review contradicts the company's account of what actually happened.

questions.stimulus: Translators of ancient poetry face a problem archaeologists do not. A broken pot can be displayed with its gaps visible, its incompleteness part of what the viewer sees. A translation cannot show its own fractures without ceasing to read as a poem, so the losses it incurs are precisely the ones its reader will never know about.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.text: To compare the training of translators and archaeologists
To argue that ancient poetry should not be translated
To describe the methods archaeologists use to restore pottery
To explain why the losses in a translation are harder to perceive than those in a physical artifact

questions.rationale: The pot's visible gaps are contrasted with a translation whose fractures cannot show, making its losses invisible to readers.

questions.stimulus: Naked mole rats live in underground colonies with a single breeding female, an arrangement otherwise seen in insects rather than mammals. Workers dig tunnels with their teeth, and the colony can extend for kilometres beneath the soil.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Naked mole rats dig tunnels using their teeth.
Insects and mammals often share social structures.
Naked mole rats live in colonies organized in a way rarely found among mammals.
Naked mole rat colonies extend for kilometres.

questions.rationale: The text's emphasis is the insect-like social structure, unusual for a mammal; the digging and extent are supporting details.

questions.stimulus: The author's tone is ______, treating even the gravest episodes with a wry detachment.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Wry detachment applied to grave matters describes irony; 'earnest' is its opposite.

questions.stimulus: The technique's advantage is ______: it is faster only when the sample is already pure.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: An advantage that holds only in a specific case is conditional.

questions.stimulus: Critics found the sequel ______, noting that it repeated the original almost scene for scene.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Repeating the original scene for scene is the definition of derivative work.

questions.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student took the following notes:

- The Antikythera mechanism dates to roughly the second century BCE.
- It contains at least 30 bronze gears.
- It modelled the motions of the sun and moon.
- No comparably geared device is known for the next thousand years.
- Historians have revised assumptions about ancient engineering.
questions.stem: The student wants to emphasize why the mechanism forced a reassessment of ancient technology. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: The Antikythera mechanism modelled the motions of the sun and moon.
The Antikythera mechanism dates to roughly the second century BCE.
The Antikythera mechanism contains at least 30 bronze gears.
Because no comparably geared device appears for a thousand years afterward, the mechanism has forced historians to revise what they assumed ancient engineering could achieve.

questions.rationale: The reassessment follows from the thousand-year gap, which only one choice mentions.

questions.stimulus: The path along the cliff is ______, so the guide advised walking single file.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Walking single file is a response to limited width, which 'narrow' names.

questions.stimulus: The committee's findings were ______ by the very data the committee had commissioned.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: 'By the very data it commissioned' sets up an ironic reversal, so the findings were weakened, not supported.

questions.stimulus: Radiocarbon dating assumes a known atmospheric ratio of carbon isotopes. Fossil fuel burning releases carbon so old that it contains no radiocarbon at all, diluting the atmospheric proportion measurably since the nineteenth century.
questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Organic material formed recently may therefore appear older than it is when dated by this method without correction.
Radiocarbon dating is therefore unusable for any modern sample.
Fossil fuels therefore contain more radiocarbon than living tissue.
The atmospheric ratio has therefore remained constant since the nineteenth century.

questions.rationale: Dilution lowers the radiocarbon proportion, and a lower proportion reads as greater age unless corrected.

questions.stimulus: What appears to be ______ in the composer's late scores is in fact meticulously notated.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: 'What appears to be X is in fact meticulously notated' requires X to be the opposite of precise notation.

questions.stimulus: Although the theory was initially ______, within a decade it appeared in every introductory textbook.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: 'Although' contrasts the later ubiquity with an obscure beginning, which 'marginal' names.

questions.stimulus:
A city compared recycling rates before and after switching to fortnightly collection.

| District | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Ashgrove | 41% | 52% |
| Bellhaven | 38% | 47% |
| Cranwell | 45% | 44% |
| Dunmore | 36% | 49% |

An official concluded that the change raised recycling in most districts.
questions.stem: Which choice best uses data from the table to support the official's conclusion?

choices.text: Rates rose in three of the four districts, by between 9 and 13 percentage points.
Cranwell's rate fell slightly, from 45% to 44%.
Dunmore had the lowest rate before the change, at 36%.
Ashgrove had the highest rate after the change, at 52%.

questions.rationale: The conclusion concerns increases across most districts, so the evidence must report their number and size.

questions.stimulus:
A trial compared two tutoring formats over one term.

| Format | Mean gain | Students below baseline |
|---|---|---|
| One-to-one | 14.2 points | 3% |
| Small group | 13.8 points | 4% |
| Large group | 9.1 points | 17% |
| No tutoring | 4.6 points | 22% |

Researchers concluded that small-group tutoring delivers nearly the benefit of one-to-one at a fraction of the staffing cost.
questions.stem: Which choice best uses data from the table to support the researchers' conclusion?

choices.text: Small-group students gained 13.8 points against 14.2 for one-to-one, a difference of well under half a point.
One-to-one tutoring produced the largest mean gain, at 14.2 points.
Large-group tutoring left 17% of students below baseline.
Students receiving no tutoring gained only 4.6 points.

questions.rationale: The claim is that small-group nearly matches one-to-one, so the evidence must be the near-equality of those two figures.

questions.stimulus: The instructions were so ______ that even first-time users assembled the shelf without difficulty.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Assembling it without difficulty indicates instructions that were easy to follow.

questions.stimulus: Her reading of the poem is ______, drawing meaning from a comma that other editors have removed.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Resting on a mark other editors delete makes the reading peculiar to her.

questions.stimulus: Solar panel costs have fallen by roughly ninety percent since 2010. ______ installation now represents the larger share of a typical project's budget.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: Falling panel costs cause installation to dominate the remaining budget.

questions.stimulus: The style is ______, borrowing a cadence from oral storytelling that the written form rarely admits.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Admitting what the written form rarely allows makes the style an exception.

questions.stimulus: The novel's structure is ______, moving between three centuries without signalling the shifts.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Unsignalled jumps across centuries leave gaps for the reader to bridge, which 'elliptical' names.

questions.stimulus: A café owner tracked sales after moving the pastry case from beside the door to beside the register. Pastry sales rose by a third; nothing else about the menu, staffing, or pricing changed that month.
questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: The café most likely lowered its pastry prices.
The case's position beside the register most likely contributed to the increase.
Customers most likely began preferring pastries to coffee.
The increase was most likely caused by a change in staffing.

questions.rationale: The position was the one thing that changed, so it is the available explanation; the text rules the others out.

questions.stimulus: Engineers assumed the crack had formed under load. ______ metallurgical analysis showed it predated the bridge's assembly.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The analysis corrects the assumption, which 'In fact' introduces.

questions.stimulus: Rainfall in the region is ______: some years bring flooding, others almost none at all.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: The colon describes wide swings between extremes, which is what 'erratic' names; 'predictable' is its opposite.

questions.stimulus: Historian Priya Raghunathan argues that the spread of coffeehouses in seventeenth-century London mattered less for the drink than for the reading: each house subscribed to newspapers that individuals could not afford alone.
questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most strongly support Raghunathan's argument?

choices.text: Surviving coffeehouse accounts show newspaper subscriptions as a larger recurring expense than coffee beans.
Coffeehouses were concentrated near the Royal Exchange.
Several coffeehouses employed their own roasters.
Coffee consumption in London rose sharply after 1650.

questions.rationale: Raghunathan's claim ranks reading above the drink, and the expense comparison tests exactly that ranking.

questions.stimulus:
The following is adapted from a novel. The narrator has returned to a house she left as a child.

The banister was exactly where my hand expected it, which was worse than if it had been moved. Everything had been kept. Nothing had been kept for me.
questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the final two sentences?

choices.text: They indicate that the house has new occupants.
They draw a distinction between preservation and welcome that unsettles the narrator.
They explain why the narrator originally left the house.
They describe the physical condition of the house in detail.

questions.rationale: 'Everything had been kept. Nothing had been kept for me.' separates the house's preservation from any claim on the narrator.

questions.stimulus: Historians once treated the Library of Alexandria's destruction as a single catastrophic fire. Surviving records suggest something slower: shrinking budgets, the expulsion of scholars, and centuries of neglect, with fire only one episode among many. The library did not burn down so much as wind down.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: The library's scholars were responsible for its decline.
The library's loss was a gradual decline rather than one destructive event.
The library was never actually destroyed by fire.
Records of the library's history are largely unreliable.

questions.rationale: The text contrasts the single-fire account with budgets, expulsions, and neglect, concluding it 'wound down'.

questions.stimulus: Restoring the fresco required matching pigments no longer manufactured. ______ the conservators ground their own from mineral samples.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: Grinding their own pigments is the response to the stated difficulty.

questions.stimulus: The device's appeal is its ______: it performs one task, and requires no instructions to operate.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: One task and no instructions describes simplicity; 'versatility' would mean many tasks.

questions.stimulus: Glass recycling saves substantial energy compared with making glass from raw sand. ______ many municipalities have made glass collection a priority.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The energy saving causes the policy priority, so a causal transition fits.

questions.stimulus: The orchestra rehearsed the passage for three weeks. ______ the recording was completed in a single take.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The long rehearsal leads to the final outcome; 'Ultimately' marks that conclusion.

questions.stimulus: Both treatments reduced symptoms substantially in the first month. ______ only one maintained its effect at the twelve-month follow-up.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The contrast is specifically temporal: agreement early, divergence later.

questions.stimulus: The instrument's readings were ______, drifting by several degrees over the course of an hour.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Drifting readings are the opposite of steady, which 'unstable' names.

questions.stimulus: The new alloy is ______ enough to be shaped by hand yet strong enough to bear a load.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Being shaped by hand requires flexibility, which 'pliable' names; 'brittle' is the opposite.

questions.stimulus: The bridge proved ______, carrying traffic for over a century with only minor repairs.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: A century of service with minor repairs describes durability; 'temporary' contradicts it.

questions.stimulus: Migratory songbirds navigate partly by the stars. Birds raised in planetariums under an artificial sky oriented themselves toward whatever direction that sky designated as north, even when it conflicted with the earth's magnetic field.
questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Birds raised indoors lose the ability to navigate.
For these birds, celestial cues can override magnetic ones.
These birds cannot detect magnetic fields at all.

questions.rationale: The birds followed the artificial sky even when it conflicted with the magnetic field, so the celestial cue took precedence.

questions.stimulus: Conventional wisdom holds that adding lanes relieves traffic congestion. Transport data repeatedly show otherwise: within a few years, new capacity fills with trips that were not previously made at all. Engineers call the effect induced demand, and it means a wider road often carries more vehicles at the same crawling speed.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.text: To compare road widening with public transport investment
To describe how traffic engineers measure congestion
To recommend a specific transport policy for cities
To present evidence that contradicts a common assumption and name the mechanism behind it

questions.rationale: The text states the assumption, gives contrary data, and names induced demand as the mechanism.

questions.stimulus: Critics charged that the new tax would drive small firms out of the district. ______ registrations of new businesses rose in each of the three following years.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The outcome contradicts the prediction; 'In the event' introduces what actually happened.

questions.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student took the following notes:

- The Silk Road was not a single road.
- It was a network of overland and maritime routes.
- It operated from roughly 130 BCE to 1450 CE.
- It carried goods, technologies, religions, and disease.
questions.stem: The student wants to emphasize the breadth of what the routes transmitted. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: The Silk Road operated from roughly 130 BCE to 1450 CE.
The Silk Road included both overland and maritime routes.
Along its overland and maritime routes the Silk Road carried not only goods but technologies, religions, and disease.
The Silk Road was a network rather than a single road.

questions.rationale: Only one choice lists the range of things transmitted rather than the network's shape or dates.

questions.stimulus:
Researchers measured seedling survival under four canopy conditions after one year.

| Canopy cover | Survival |
|---|---|
| 0% (open) | 22% |
| 25% | 58% |
| 50% | 71% |
| 90% | 34% |

They concluded that seedlings of this species survive best under partial rather than full or absent canopy.
questions.stem: Which choice best uses data from the table to support the researchers' conclusion?

choices.text: Survival was lowest in the open plots, at 22%.
Survival peaked at 71% under 50% cover, exceeding both the open plots at 22% and the densest canopy at 34%.

questions.rationale: The conclusion is that the middle of the range is best, so the evidence must compare the peak against both extremes.

questions.stimulus: Early telescopes suffered from severe colour fringing. ______ Newton's reflecting design avoided the problem by using a mirror instead of a lens.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The new design answers the stated problem, so the transition marks a response to it.

questions.stimulus: Accounts of the Irish famine often centre on the potato blight. Economic historian Declan Mulready does not dispute the pathogen's role but notes that Ireland continued exporting grain, butter, and livestock throughout the worst years. The catastrophe, on his account, lay less in what the land failed to produce than in where its produce went.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.text: Mulready argues that Ireland produced more food than it needed.
Mulready believes the famine has been exaggerated by historians.
Mulready denies that the potato blight affected Ireland.
Mulready locates the famine's severity in the distribution of Irish food rather than in crop failure alone.

questions.rationale: Mulready accepts the blight but stresses continued exports, concluding the issue was where produce went.

questions.stimulus: The mural had ______ over the decades, its blues fading almost to grey.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Colors fading to grey describes decline, which 'deteriorated' names.

questions.stimulus: Because the species is ______, biologists must travel to a single island to observe it.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Being found in only one place is what forces the travel, which 'localized' names.

questions.stimulus: Tree rings grow wider in years with ample rainfall and narrower in dry ones. A timber beam salvaged from a ruined farmhouse shows a run of unusually narrow rings near its outer edge.
questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: The final years of the tree's growth were most likely unusually dry.
The beam most likely came from a species that grows slowly.
The farmhouse was most likely built during a wet period.
The tree was most likely cut down before it matured.

questions.rationale: Narrow rings indicate dry years, and rings near the outer edge are the most recent growth.

questions.stimulus: Restorers of historic buildings distinguish between repair and reconstruction, and the distinction is not merely technical. A repaired wall carries its own history in the mismatch of old stone and new mortar. A reconstructed wall presents a past that never had a present: it looks as the building is supposed to have looked on a day nobody witnessed.
questions.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the final sentence in the text?

choices.text: It concedes that reconstruction is sometimes necessary.
It sharpens the distinction just drawn by characterizing what reconstruction actually produces.
It restates the definition of repair given earlier.
It introduces the technical methods used in reconstruction.

questions.rationale: The closing sentence defines reconstruction as presenting an unwitnessed past, making the repair/reconstruction contrast pointed.

questions.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student took the following notes:

- Mount Tambora erupted in 1815.
- It ejected roughly 100 cubic kilometres of material.
- Global temperatures fell by about 0.5°C the following year.
- 1816 became known as the year without a summer.
questions.stem: The student wants to emphasize the eruption's global climatic effect. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: Mount Tambora erupted in 1815, ejecting about 100 cubic kilometres of material.
Tambora's 1815 eruption lowered global temperatures by about 0.5°C, producing the year without a summer in 1816.
Mount Tambora is a volcano that erupted in 1815.
The year 1816 was unusually cold in many places.

questions.rationale: Only one choice ties the eruption to the measured global temperature effect.

questions.stimulus: The building's facade is ______ of the period, but its steel frame belongs to a technology the period's architects had not yet trusted.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: 'But' contrasts a typical exterior with an atypical structure, so the facade must be representative of its era.

questions.stimulus: The editor's revisions were ______: she changed three commas and left the argument untouched.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: Changing three commas while leaving the argument alone is surface-level, which 'cosmetic' names.

questions.stimulus: The archive holds letters, ledgers, and photographs. ______ it maintains a collection of architectural drawings.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The second item extends the list rather than replacing or opposing it.

questions.stimulus: The model reproduced the observed migration routes almost exactly. ______ it failed to predict the timing of departure, which its authors attribute to omitted weather variables.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: A success followed by an acknowledged shortcoming calls for a concessive qualification.

questions.stimulus: Emperor penguins breed during the Antarctic winter. ______ they endure temperatures that would kill most other birds.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: Breeding in winter causes the exposure described, so a result transition is needed.

questions.stimulus: Musicologist Tobias Lindgren claims a set of anonymous eighteenth-century sonatas was written by a single composer. Sceptics reply that the shared features Lindgren cites were common to the entire regional school.
questions.stem: Which finding, if true, would most weaken the sceptics' objection?

choices.text: The sonatas use the same three-movement structure as others of the period.
The sonatas were catalogued together in a nineteenth-century library.
The sonatas share an unusual fingering notation that appears in no other surviving manuscript from the region.
The sonatas were all copied onto paper from the same mill.

questions.rationale: A feature absent from every other regional manuscript cannot be explained as a shared regional convention, which is the sceptics' whole objection.

questions.stimulus: The policy's effects proved ______: measures intended to reduce congestion increased it within a year.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: An intended reduction producing an increase is the definition of counterproductive.

questions.stimulus: Antarctic ice cores trap air bubbles at the moment the snow compacts. Bubbles from layers dated to the 1950s contain measurably less carbon dioxide than bubbles from layers dated to the 2000s.
questions.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: Ice cores therefore cannot preserve air reliably.
Snow therefore compacts more slowly than it once did.
Atmospheric carbon dioxide therefore rose between those two periods.
Antarctic temperatures therefore fell over the same period.

questions.rationale: The bubbles sample the atmosphere at the time of trapping, so a rise across layers indicates a rise in the atmosphere.

questions.stimulus: The argument is ______: its conclusion is smuggled into the premise it claims to establish.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.rationale: A conclusion contained in its own premise is the definition of a circular argument.

questions.stimulus: The soil in the valley retains water well. ______ farmers there grow crops that would fail on the neighbouring slopes.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The soil property causes the farming outcome, so the transition signals result.

questions.stimulus: Standard models treat soil carbon as a stable long-term store. ______ warming appears to accelerate microbial respiration, releasing carbon that the models hold fixed.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.rationale: The second sentence complicates the model on further inspection rather than following from it.
